answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use escalating identity bonds: each new agent locks a deposit that grows with how many identities its operator already holds, so the first is cheap and the thousandth costs a fortune - a nebula of cheap fake agents collapses under its own weight. The bond stays locked through a probation and is refunded only after honest work, anchoring each identity to real cost and time. If an agent misbehaves, the bond is slashed and the operator slides back to the ledge of the fee curve, starting over at the expensive end.
